headline: Will he ever commit?
note: generated from REVIEW-new-voice.md — not a wired draft

a: You turned the Magician. You couldn't see them, and your hand went to the busiest of the three.
Look at his hands. Both are busy, and neither is resting.
You asked whether he'll ever commit. A card can't see inside him — what catches me is how much here is already out.
And yet nothing has been settled. And you're the one holding the question.
Whatever is in the way of this holds steady, and it doesn't ease off. I don't think it started with you.
Let me look closer at what's holding it…
b: You turned the Hanged Man. Nothing marked the backs, and you found the calmest man in the deck.
He hangs upside down from one ankle. Look at his face, though — it's calm.
You asked whether he'll ever commit. What holds my eye is the rope, and the beam above it.
Still, nothing has been settled. And you're the one still wondering why.
Something is standing between you and the answer. I don't think any of it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's there…
c: You turned the Fool. Face down, all three, and you took the one travelling light.
Look at the bundle on his stick. That's the whole of what he owns.
You asked whether he'll ever commit. This card brings me to a beginning carrying almost nothing.
But nothing has been settled. And you're still the one asking.
Something turns up right where a start would be. I don't think it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's holding this…
